claims.claim: AT&T reported second-quarter 2026 revenues of $31.6 billion.
Revenues were up 2.3% year over year.
The quarter included record combined fiber and fixed wireless net adds.
AT&T reiterated all consolidated full-year 2026 and multi-year guidance.
AT&T is raising the pace of 2026 share repurchases to approximately $10 billion.
Revenues were $31.6 billion versus $30.8 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Operating expenses were $24.5 billion versus $24.3 billion in the year-ago quarter.
Operating income was $7.0 billion versus $6.5 billion.
Adjusted operating income (non-GAAP) was $7.5 billion versus $6.5 billion.
Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $0.66 versus $0.62.
Adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) was $0.65 versus $0.54.
Income from continuing operations was $5.0 billion, up 3.6%.
Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $12.3 billion, up 5.2%.
Cash from operating activities from continuing operations was $10.8 billion versus $9.8 billion.
Capital expenditures were $5.7 billion versus $4.9 billion.
Capital investment (non-GAAP) was $6.1 billion versus $5.1 billion.
Free cash flow (non-GAAP) was $4.7 billion versus $4.4 billion.
Advanced Connectivity operating revenues were $28,615 million, up 4.1%.
Advanced Connectivity service revenue was $23,478 million, up 5.1%.
Advanced home internet revenue rose 27.3% to $2,926 million.
Wireless service revenue rose 3.3%.
Advanced Connectivity segment operating income was $7,345 million, up 20.3%.
Advanced Connectivity segment EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $12,032 million, up 8.0%.
Internet net adds were 646,000, comprised of 367,000 fiber and 279,000 fixed wireless.
Postpaid phone net adds were 432,000.
Postpaid phone churn was 0.86%.
AT&T added over 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers in the quarter.
Total consumer and business locations reached with fiber totaled 38.6 million.
42.5% of advanced home internet households also took AT&T wireless.
Legacy segment revenues fell 25.9% to $1,632 million.
Legacy operating income and EBITDA (non-GAAP) were $523 million, down $436 million year over year.
Latin America revenues rose 16.1% to $1,224 million.
Latin America revenue growth was driven by favorable foreign exchange and postpaid subscriber growth.
Latin America operating income was $38 million, down $8 million.
Latin America EBITDA (non-GAAP) was $227 million, up $26 million.
2026 guidance includes adjusted EPS (non-GAAP) of $2.25 to $2.35.
2026 guidance includes adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) growth of 3% to 4%.
2026 guidance includes free cash flow (non-GAAP) of $18 billion or more.
2026 guidance includes Advanced Connectivity service revenue growth of 5% or more.
The 2026-2028 outlook includes low-single-digit annual service revenue growth.
The 2026-2028 outlook includes capital investment (non-GAAP) of $23 billion to $24 billion annually.
The outlook includes free cash flow (non-GAAP) of $19 billion+ in 2027 and $21 billion+ in 2028.
AT&T plans to return $45 billion or more to shareholders during 2026-2028.
Total debt was $144.0 billion.
Net debt (non-GAAP) was $126.4 billion.
Cash and cash equivalents were $17.6 billion.
AT&T returned $4.1 billion to shareholders in the quarter.
That included approximately $2.2 billion of common share repurchases under the 2024 authorization.
AT&T plans to maintain its current annualized common stock dividend of $1.11 per share.
Operating expenses included an asset abandonment charge associated with reprioritization of the Company's spectrum strategy.
Reported diluted EPS included a $0.05 benefit from tax items and a $0.03 asset abandonment charge, per the company's reconciliation.
The acquired Lumen fiber network subsidiary is classified as held-for-sale and reflected as discontinued operations, with AT&T planning to sell a controlling interest to an equity partner.
AT&T expects net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA to return to its 2.5x target range within approximately three years following the closing of the EchoStar transaction.
